sections.explanation: Training captures are separate runs. A short instrumented epoch must not be substituted for historical full-training epoch time. Evaluation uses its recorded split and averaging policy.
sections.title: Training and evaluation

sections.explanation: Latency is a batch forward duration. Throughput counts completed images in a wall window. E2E also includes acquisition, queueing and postprocessing; their clocks and denominators stay separate.
sections.title: Inference latency and throughput

sections.explanation: Process RSS includes runtime and allocator effects. Registered tensor logical bytes, serialized file size and CUDA allocator counters describe different quantities, not one interchangeable memory total.
sections.title: Memory and footprint

sections.explanation: Logical FLOPs/MACs describe the declared operation convention and observed coverage. Profiler time includes instrumentation. Payload estimates do not establish native DRAM traffic or a qualified hardware roof.
sections.title: FLOPs and profiling

sections.explanation: Quality belongs to the recorded cohort and class mapping. Perturbation/precision experiments use paired samples. Percentage points differ from relative percent; observed Pareto is not independently verified improvement.
sections.title: Quality, robustness and precision

sections.explanation: Device and backend conditions must match before comparisons. Provider availability is not evidence that a graph node executed there. Missing devices and ambiguous node mappings remain explicit.
sections.title: Hardware and runtime

sections.explanation: A completed short window is not long-duration acceptance. RSS growth alone is not a causal memory leak. Energy requires actual compatible sensor samples, not a TDP or utilization estimate.
sections.title: Stability and energy
